summary: Heavy steel lookout with octagonal cupola, built 1958 in eastern Ontario; district towers phased out in the 1970s; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Heavy steel tower with an octagonal cupola
facts.status_note: No source found says whether the tower still stands.
facts.agency: Ontario Department of Lands and Forests

events.note: Year built is given as 1958 in the firelookout.ca entry.
Shown on the Department of Lands and Forests Tower Detection System Map.
Shown on Pembroke topographic map 31F, 3rd ed.; the entry says it also appears in the current 4th edition.

evidence.supports: Listed site on Black Creek Road, North Algona Wilberforce, in Eastern Ontario
evidence.quote: Black Creek Road, North Algona Wilberforce, Renfrew County, Eastern Ontario, Ontario

evidence.supports: Heavy steel, octagonal cupola, total cost $3,709.52, Canada Bridge Co. Ltd. named
evidence.quote: Heavy steel; Canada Bridge Co. Ltd.;octagonal cupola total cost $3,709.52;

evidence.supports: Shown on the 1963 Department of Lands and Forests Tower Detection System Map
evidence.quote: Appears on the Department of Lands and Forests Tower Detection System Map (1963)

evidence.supports: Shown on Pembroke topographic map 31F, 1977, and in the current 4th edition
evidence.quote: Appears on Pembroke topographic map 31F, 3rd ed., 1977 and in current 4th

evidence.supports: Pembroke Forest Fire District founded in 1922 by the Department of Lands and Forests
evidence.quote: The Pembroke Forest Fire District was founded by Ontario's former Department of Lands and Forests (now the MNR) in 1922

evidence.supports: District headquarters were in the town of Pembroke
evidence.quote: The headquarters for the district were housed in the town.

evidence.supports: Wilberforce is one of 15 lookouts the district served
evidence.quote: The 15 towers included: Wilberforce, Mt. Edna, Sherwood, Murchison

evidence.supports: Towermen radioed bearings to headquarters, where they could be combined to plot a fire
evidence.quote: When a fire was spotted in the forest a towerman would get the degree bearings from his respective tower and radio back the information to headquarters.

evidence.supports: Bearings from more than one tower could place the fire on a map (triangulation)
evidence.quote: When one or more towermen from other towers in the area would also call in their bearings, the forest rangers at headquarters could get a 'triangulation' read and plot the exact location of the fire on their map.

evidence.supports: District towers phased out after aerial firefighting came into use in the 1970s
evidence.quote: These towers would all be phased out after aerial fire fighting techniques were employed in the 1970s.

notes_for_editor: Build year, design and cupola details rest on one volunteer-submitted firelookout.ca entry. No source found says when the tower came down or what remains today, so the story says so. Wikipedia gives only the 1970s for the district's phase-out, so no year-level end event is recorded. The 4th-edition remark concerns a map, not the structure. Brief name, elevation and coordinates match firelookout.ca. Two web searches found no other source on this tower; a Renfrew County or Ontario forestry or heritage search may still find the removal date.
